items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.

items.summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.
items.title: The Inverse Berggren Tree Problem

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).

items.summary: Supplementary data and code accompanying the manuscript “An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach”. This package provides materials for editors and referees to check the study’s methods and results. It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. The study synthesizes published historical sources, museum catalogues, and publicly disclosed institutional records. No new laboratory, survey, or interview datasets were generated. Author-generated materials are shared under CC BY 4.0; copyrighted verbatim text of published sources is cited but not reproduced in full. Natural Earth data are public domain.

items.summary: Replication package for the journal article on attributing LLM-paraphrased source code to the model that produced it, in the setting where someone has an LLM rewrite code that another person wrote so that it no longer looks copied. Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.
items.title: STACAD: replication package for 'Attributing paraphrased source code to the large language model that rewrote it'

items.summary: This repository provides the compiled analysis inputs, R code, figure source data and GIS rasters supporting the manuscript “Historical introduction pools pre-structure future plant invasion debt under climate change”. Version 2.0 contains the final USA-intersection climatic-analogue reconstruction and its corresponding model predictions and spatial summaries. The historical introduction pool contains 18,562 species. The stage-transition models use 5,791 complete-case species, of which 4,088 species without a recorded invasion form the future candidate invasion-debt subset. Future predictions cover 12 combinations of two climate scenarios (SSP126 and SSP585), three periods (2041–2060, 2061–2080 and 2081–2100), and two global climate models (HadGEM3-GC31-LL and MPI-ESM1-2-HR). The archive contains: • Figure_data: XLSX source workbooks for main Figures 1–4, Supplementary Figures S1–S4 and Supplementary Tables S1–S15, together with the compiled species-level analysis dataset and current and future candidate-species predictions. • Code: R scripts, computational inputs and provenance documentation for the stage-transition models, climatic-analogue searches, future predictions, phylogenetic null analysis, temporal analyses, sensitivity analyses and publication source tables. • GIS_rasters: GeoTIFFs for the main and supplementary spatial figures. Main Figure 4 rasters contain sums within globally aligned 0.5° display cells; supplementary spatial rasters retain the native 10-arc-minute resolution. • Validation: execution records and numerical checks. • README files: instructions for reproducing the analyses, plotting the source data and interpreting the spatial fields. Current and future closest US climatic analogue cells are identified separately for each candidate species. POT is the sum of future predicted invasion probabilities assigned to future analogue cells. CHG is future grid-level transition potential minus current grid-level transition potential, with unassigned cells completed with zero. CHG therefore incorporates both changes in predicted probability and relocation of climatic analogues. POSDP is the sum of positive species-level changes assigned to future analogue cells; Supplementary Figure S3 reports its range across the two climate models. The analytical workflow was tested with R 4.3.3. Reproduction starts from the compiled historical master dataset, supplied phylogenetic inputs, prepared species climatic centroids and extracted WorldClim grid values. items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.

items.summary: Rank Access and Closure Depth in the Relation-Layer Cohomology of Token Arenas A refuted conjecture, a refuted mechanism, and two species of invariant harmonic residue     Driven by Dean Kulik October 2026     Abstract A K disj -type relation layer over a token arena assigns cohomology to a graph by declaring which closed loops count as relations. We settle an open problem about such layers and then identify what actually governs them. First, the conjecture that two vertex orbits force ε harm ( K 4 ) = 0 is refuted by an exact 12-vertex counterexample with |Aut| = 24, reproduced by two implementations whose constructions of the invariant cochain space share no logic. Second, we localize the failure: it is not a shortage of cells. On the witness's two-dimensional residue, all 1083 arena 4-cycles supply rank 1, while 20 arena 3-cycles of an excluded shape supply rank 2, and the two nonzero square families have the same image, a single line. Third, we refute the natural mechanism for this — that the residue is an odd-cycle blind spot — by exhibiting bipartite arenas, containing no odd cycle of any length, that still carry residue. The operative property is omission from the declared family, not parity. Fourth, we prove that ε harm ( K 3,4 ) > 0 on an infinite family — every cycle graph with n ≥ 5 and 2 ≤ K ≤ n−1, under the trivial group and the rotation subgroup, and zero under the full dihedral group — answering a question the odd-cycle reading had posed. Fifth, we define closure depth L closure , prove it exceeds 4 for every member of that family, and measure it as exactly n for C n and 4 for the witness, so no short vocabulary closes the family. This separates two populated regimes: residue a longer reader dissolves, and residue carried by configuration-space topology. Finally we identify the second kind. At trivial group the framework's own quantity is simplicial H 1 over ℚ , and the declared cells are the 2-skeleton of Abrams' discretized configuration space; the cell counts and Euler characteristic are verified against closed form, Abrams' subdivision hypothesis for C n reduces to n ≥ K + 1, the measured rank is 1 on all 33 admissible rows and 0 on all 8 excluded boundary rows, and the equivariant degree is solved exactly: +1 for rotations, −1 for reflections. All arithmetic is exact rational. Keywords: graph configuration space, graph braid group, token graph, discrete Morse theory, equivariant cohomology, cube complex, relation layer, closure depth MSC 2020: 55R80, 05C10, 20F36, 55N91, 05C85 License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Source code and executed notebook accompany this paper; see Appendix B. 1. Introduction A graph does not come with a cohomology. One is obtained by declaring a relation layer: a set of closed loops in some derived space that are stipulated to bound. Change the declaration and the cohomology changes while the graph does not. This paper is about what that dependence actually is, measured rather than described. The derived space here is a token arena . Fix a finite simple graph X , an integer K ≥ 1, and a group G ≤ Aut( X ). The arena A K ( X ) has the K -element subsets of V ( X ) as vertices, with an edge whenever two subsets differ by moving one token along one edge of X . A relation layer declares a family of arena loops as 2-cells; the G -invariant cochain complex of the resulting 2-complex has a first cohomology whose dimension we write ε harm . The quantity is relative to the declaration, and that is the point. Two declarations are natural and were already in use. K disj admits only commuting squares : two token moves along base edges with disjoint closed supports, which therefore commute. K 4 admits every 4-cycle of the arena. Since K disj ⊆ K 4 , monotonicity gives ε harm ( K 4 ) ≤ ε harm ( K disj ), and the interesting question is when the larger family closes what the smaller one l

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). items.summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. Version 1.1.0 contains 9,048 unique question-hop instances derived from four ontology datasets: Family, Pizza 100, Pizza 250, and OWL2Bench. The benchmark contains 6,032 binary question-answering (BQA) instances and 3,016 open-ended question-answering (OEQA) instances. Benchmark instances support 1-hop and 2-hop ontology contexts and aligned natural-language (NL), formal-symbolic (FS), and entity-abstracted (AR) representations. Ground-truth answers and explanation structures are derived using symbolic ontology reasoning, enabling controlled evaluation according to task formulation, representation, semantic abstraction, context depth, explanation-based reasoning complexity, and reasoning type. The release includes benchmark data, reasoning metadata, provenance and licensing documentation, release manifests and checksums, and scripts supporting benchmark generation, validation, Hugging Face export, and reproducibility. The canonical source-code release is CORE-LLM-Bench v1.1.0 on GitHub. Licensing is component-specific. Repository software is MIT licensed; separable original CORE-LLM-Bench benchmark content is CC BY 4.0; Pizza-derived material follows CC BY 3.0; OWL2Bench-derived material follows Apache-2.0; and Family/FHKB-derived material follows CC BY-SA 3.0.
